sentences.english_text: Far back in the theater, crouched in a corner was a mouse.
The mouse was crouched in a corner because it did not want to be seen.
Nobody likes to have a mouse in a theater, and the mouse knew that if they saw him, they would try to catch him.
So he stayed out of sight, watching the show.
Now the mouse had very sharp eyes.
The audience could not see Drippy on the stage because he was so small.
But as Drippy was spinning around on top of the ball that the seal was playing with, the mouse saw Drippy.
And he recognized him.
That's Drippy, the one-away waintrop.
Everybody in the world has been looking for him.
And I found him.
The trick is to get him back home to his mother.
The mouse was not sure how to do that.
He thought about it for a long time.
Then he got an idea.
Very quietly, careful not to be seen, the mouse crept downstairs to the basement where his friend the Cricket was.
And the mouse said to the Cricket, I found Drippy.
The Cricket was amazed.
You did?
Where is he?
He's upstairs on the stage.
We have to get him back to his mother.
How do we do that?
They both stood there thinking.
Then the Cricket said, I have an idea.
And the Cricket hurried out to the street where he saw a bluebird.
We found Drippy.
That's wonderful.
His mother will be so happy.
Where is he?
He's inside the theater on the stage.
Can you go into the theater and get him and fly him to his mother?
The bluebird thought for a long time.
Then he said, No, little Cricket.
They would never allow a bluebird into the theater.
What are we going to do?
The bluebird said, I'll fly to Mrs. Dewdrop and tell her the news.
She can figure out how to get him home.
And the bluebird quickly flew off to where Mrs. Dewdrop was.
